Every Blastocystis SSU rRNA record on GenBank, curated and audited

The figures from the talk, with the underlying tables live underneath them — 1,052 audited reference sequences drawn from 18,074 public records, August 2026.

Step one

From 18,074 records to an audited set of 1,052

One genus-wide query, then content validation rather than trust in the deposited labels. The largest cut is length: the ~600 bp barcode amplicons cannot resolve recent subtype splits, so they are set aside for a separate analysis rather than discarded.

18,074records retrieved
1,274near-full-length (1,000–2,500 bp)
222cross-label duplicates removed
1,052final reference set
62distinct labels
92.7%confidently assigned

Those 62 labels break down as 43 accepted or tentative subtypes covering 975 records, 18 provisional novel clusters covering 50, and 27 singletons left deliberately unassigned.

Finding

Subtypes are real, separable clusters

Across the 975 records carrying an accepted subtype label, sequences sit about six times closer to their own subtype than to any other. The ordination is the illustration; the distance distributions are the evidence.

0.021median within a subtype
0.121median between subtypes
5.8×ratio
−0.981Cliff's δ
474,825pairwise comparisons
43 accepted or tentative subtypes · click a header to sort

Control

Sanger built this database — and technology doesn't distort it

Sanger still supplies well over half the reference set. The question that matters is whether the platform mix bends the subtype structure, so the test compares same-platform against mixed-platform pairs drawn from within the same subtype.

Mixing technologies moves the within-subtype median from 0.021 to 0.024 — a shift of three thousandths against the 0.100 gap that separates subtypes, with Cliff's δ of −0.13, a negligible effect.

What the record samples

Humans, pigs — and one odd iguana batch

About a third of host-annotated records are human, and the expected biology falls out without being asked for: ST1 and ST3 in humans, ST5 and ST12 in pigs, the artiodactyl subtypes in sheep and cattle. One pairing does not belong.

307human records (32%)
111 / 88human ST1 / ST3
157pig records
71 of 74ST11 records are iguanas
The flag. All 71 iguana records in ST11 — a subtype otherwise associated with elephants — come from a single submission batch, one deposit from Thailand in 2022. The sequences place there cleanly, but an unusual host–subtype pairing resting on one deposit is exactly what an audit exists to surface.

What the record samples

The map follows the sequencers, not the organism

Thailand and China lead, but the shape of this panel is set by who deposited, not by where the parasite lives. Several countries are represented by a single submission — Peru and Denmark entirely so.

28countries with records
0African records
74largest single deposit
143country not recorded
345carry a collection date
Sort by “% largest” to see which countries are really one deposit
Africa is a flat zero. Twenty-eight countries appear among the records with a recorded country, and not one of them is in Africa. For a parasite this prevalent in humans, that is a gap in the reference database, not in the biology — and it will look identical next year unless labs with material deposit near-full-length sequences.

Finding

Ninety records match no accepted subtype

They resolve into 18 provisional clusters plus 27 singletons. Most carry the signature of one submission batch that simply dropped its subtype tag — one host, one country, one deposit. The diagnostic is metadata breadth, not how tight the cluster is.

Filled pills mark more than one distinct value · “–” means not recorded
Two are flagged, on different evidence. The chelonian lineage (novel 3) is the one that clears the metadata test outright: six tortoise species, two countries, two unrelated submissions, plus 12 barcode records from five further countries. The Castor fiber cluster (novel 10) does not clear it — it is metadata-thin — and is flagged instead because it is near-full-length, appeared only in 2026 deposits, and drew an independent high-confidence match from Slovakia. Cluster labels are clustering output, not taxonomy; they renumber between runs.

The other 16,000 records

The barcode corpus, mapped back — and it votes

The short records excluded from the reference set were subtype-called separately against it by k-mer containment. They cannot define a new lineage under current standards, but they can corroborate one.

16,784barcode records
92.8%confidently called
121landed in novel clusters
11 of 18clusters corroborated

The barcode world is human-surveillance shaped: ST3 holds 26.6% of barcode records against 15.6% of the full-length set, while reference-oriented sequencing over-represents ST1 and the animal subtypes.
